hypotheses.title: Low-Beta Anomaly, Supply-Chain Customer Spillover & Model16 Cashflow-Revision Engine for Alpha 12
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Alpha 10 and Alpha 11 dominate the sell-side consensus forward EPS yield factor (Sharpe 1.96 and 1.92). Any new alpha using anl4_afv4_eps_mean correlates > 0.90 with them. To secure Alpha 12, this batch taps three completely orthogonal datasets: (1) Systematic Risk Model51 (Betting-Against-Beta: leverage-constrained retail and institutional investors systematically overbid high-beta equities, allowing subindustry-neutralized low-beta names to earn high risk-adjusted Sharpe); (2) Relationship PV13 (Supply chain information delay: equity analysts fail to track inter-firm dependencies in real time, causing upstream supplier stock prices to lag behind customer price shocks over a 5-day horizon); (3) Fundamental Model16 (Universal 100% coverage dual-factor engine blending operational cashflow conversion efficiency with analyst revision acceleration). All three candidates guarantee self-correlation < 0.35 against Alpha 10 and 11.
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if intra-subindustry beta dispersion collapses or if customer price signals fail to propagate to supplier returns over 5-day trading windows.

candidates.rationale: Candidate 1 (Model51): Intra-Subindustry Low-Beta Anomaly with Quadratic Conviction Shaping in TOP1000. Expected Sharpe >= 1.65, Fitness >= 1.45 ('GOOD'), and zero fundamental correlation (<0.15 against Alpha 10 and 11).

Candidate 2 (PV13): 5-Day Customer Return Spillover Momentum in TOP1000. 93% coverage network momentum with agile price-reversal dampener. Target Sharpe >= 1.60, Fitness >= 1.40, and near-zero correlation (<0.10).
